assumptions: System A axioms A1-A3
alphabet sizes 2-4
words of bounded length (exact, since the relations preserve length)
new.falsification: Any slice where a class contains two words with different projections, or two words with equal projections lie in different classes, or completion fails/normal form differs.
new.hypothesis: Two words are congruent iff, for every symbol s, deleting all other symbols gives the same word s...s (equal symbol projections). The shortlex-completed system {yx -> xy : x < y} is finite and its normal forms are the sorted words.
new.methodology: For every alphabet/length slice, compute the exact congruence classes by union-find over single swap steps; compare the partition with the projection partition; run shortlex Knuth-Bendix completion and compare normal forms with sorted words.
new.question: In System A with the swap relations xy <-> yx, what distinguishes two words that cannot be transformed into each other?
new.title: Commutation congruence: classes, complete invariant and normal forms

assumptions: System A, alphabet {a}
exponents are meta-level names for unary numerals
relations with 1-3 equations and exponents <= 20
new.falsification: Any relation set where completion yields a different rule, the class count differs from M + P, or the bounded union-find partition of small exponents differs from the formula.
new.hypothesis: The congruence generated by relations a^{m_i} = a^{n_i} (m_i < n_i) is the monogenic congruence with index M = min m_i and period P = gcd(n_i - m_i): exactly M + P classes, a^x ~ a^y iff x = y or (x, y >= M and x = y mod P).
new.methodology: Two independent methods per relation set: (1) shortlex Knuth-Bendix completion, reading index/period from the completed single rule and counting irreducible words; (2) union-find over exponents 0..B with all shifted relations (B = 6 max n). Compare both with the formula.
new.question: What structures arise when words over a single symbol a are identified by finitely many relations a^m = a^n?
new.title: One-symbol congruences: index and period of finitely generated congruences

assumptions: System A over {a} and over {a,b} modulo commutation
finite window of images
new.falsification: Any failure of a semiring axiom, or commuting compositions for all two-symbol samples.
new.hypothesis: Endomorphisms of {a}* (substitutions a -> w) with pointwise juxtaposition (f+g)(u) = f(u)g(u) and composition form a commutative semiring isomorphic to (N, +, x) via f -> f(a). With two symbols modulo commutation, composition is no longer commutative.
new.methodology: Represent an endomorphism by the image of a (a word). Implement substitution and juxtaposition on strings only; check every semiring axiom on all images a^0..a^K; check the length map is a homomorphism. For {a,b}/commutation, sample substitutions and look for non-commuting compositions.
new.question: Is there a second operation on unary numerals that arises from transformations alone?
new.title: Endomorphisms of the one-symbol free monoid form the semiring of natural numbers

assumptions: System A over {a,b}
relations of length 3 and 4
words of length <= 11
new.falsification: A word of length >= |u| whose class is strictly smaller than its Parikh class.
new.hypothesis: H-C01-4 (inventor's conjecture, deliberately bold): for every relation u <-> v over {a,b} with u != v and equal symbol counts, the generated congruence coincides with Parikh equivalence on all words of length >= |u|.
new.methodology: For each relation (up to swapping sides) compute exact congruence classes of each length (length-preserving, so exact), and compare their number and content with Parikh classes.
new.question: If a relation u <-> v only rearranges symbols, does it eventually identify all words with the same symbol counts (on long enough words)?
new.title: Single Parikh-preserving relations versus the Parikh (counting) equivalence

assumptions: System A
alphabets of size 2 (k = 2..5, n <= 12) and 3 (k = 2..3, n <= 7)
exact classes (relations preserve length)
new.falsification: Any relation with an unbordered side whose class counts differ from the series.
new.hypothesis: H-C01-5: if |u| = |v| = k, u != v and u is unbordered (no proper prefix equals a suffix), then the number of classes of length-n words over a q-letter alphabet equals [x^n] 1/(1 - q x + x^k), i.e. the number of length-n words avoiding u.
new.methodology: Exhaustive over all unordered pairs {u, v} of distinct words of length k. Exact class counts by union-find; compare with the series coefficients; for relations whose sides are both bordered, record counts, the minimal linear recurrence fitted to them, and whether shortlex completion terminates.
new.question: Why do all length-3 relations give F(n+3)-1 classes and most length-4 relations give partial sums of tribonacci numbers? Which relations are exceptions?
new.title: Class counts modulo one relation u <-> v: the unbordered-side theorem and its exceptions

assumptions: System A; length-preserving single relations u != v
binary k = 2..6 (n <= 12, k = 6 restricted to 'hard' pairs), ternary k = 2..4 (n <= 7, k = 4 restricted to hard pairs)
new.falsification: Any relation whose exact class counts differ from the formula.
new.hypothesis: H-C01-7: with k = |u| = |v|, q = alphabet size and c(x) = 1 + sum over words b that are borders of both u and v of x^(k-|b|), the class counts are the coefficients of c(x) / (x^k + (1 - q x) c(x)) (= the number of length-n words avoiding any single word whose autocorrelation is c).
new.methodology: Exact class counts by union-find. 'Hard' pairs are those where neither border set contains the other (the case not covered by the proved containment theorem); for k <= 5 binary and k <= 3 ternary all pairs are tested.
new.question: Is the number of classes of length-n words modulo u <-> v determined by the common borders of u and v?
new.title: Common-border formula for one-relation class counts (test on old and new cases)

assumptions: Newman's lemma and the critical-pair lemma for string rewriting
Cayley-Hamilton bound on the order of DFA count recurrences
new.falsification: A verified convergent completion whose irreducible-word counts differ from the formula would refute H-C01-7 for that relation.
new.hypothesis: For most small relations some shortlex order (alphabet permutation, read left-to-right or right-to-left) yields a finite convergent completion; its irreducible words then give a rational count sequence that can be compared with the formula exactly.
new.methodology: For each relation and each of 2*q! shortlex orders: run bounded Knuth-Bendix; on success, independently re-verify convergence (rules decreasing, all critical pairs joinable, u and v have equal normal forms); build the Aho-Corasick DFA of the left-hand sides (s live states); compare s + k + 5 count terms with the formula (sufficient for equality of all terms); cross-check against brute-force class counts for n <= 8.
new.question: For which relations u <-> v can H-C01-7 be proved for ALL lengths n by a finite certificate?
new.title: Automatic proofs of the common-border class-count formula via finite completion

new.applications: Linear-time decision of equality modulo commutation; justifies introducing N in System C.
new.novelty_basis: Free commutative monoid on Sigma is N^Sigma (Parikh vectors, Parikh 1966); special case of Mazurkiewicz trace monoids (Cartier-Foata 1969).
new.proof_check: Lean 4 + Mathlib (commEq_iff_count, projection_is_unary); standard axioms only
new.statement:
Two words over a finite alphabet are congruent modulo the swap relations xy = yx iff every symbol occurs
equally often in both; the projection of a word onto a symbol s is the unary word s...s of that length.
new.title: Symbol counts are the complete invariant of the commutation congruence

new.novelty_basis: Index and period of monogenic semigroups (e.g. Howie 1995, Fundamentals of Semigroup Theory).
new.proof_check: Lean 4 + Mathlib (gen_iff, exactly_m_add_p_classes); standard axioms only
new.statement:
On one-symbol words, a^x ~ a^y modulo a^m = a^(m+p) (p >= 1) iff nf(x) = nf(y) with nf(x) = x for x < m and
m + ((x - m) mod p) otherwise; there are exactly m + p classes.
new.title: One symbol, one relation a^m = a^(m+p) gives exactly m+p classes (index m, period p)

new.novelty_basis: Standard description of finitely generated congruences on (N,+) / cyclic semigroups.
new.proof_check: written proof (proofs/paper/C01.md, Theorem 3); computationally corroborated on 6159 relation sets; awaiting independent skeptic review
new.statement:
The congruence on {a}* generated by a^(m_i) = a^(n_i) (m_i < n_i, i = 1..r) identifies a^x and a^y iff
x = y or (x, y >= M and P | x - y), where M = min m_i and P = gcd(n_i - m_i); it has M + P classes.
new.title: Several one-symbol relations have index min m_i and period gcd(n_i - m_i)

new.novelty_basis: Endomorphism semiring of (N,+) is (N,+,x); endomorphisms of N^2 are 2x2 matrices over N.
new.proof_check: written proof (proofs/paper/C01.md, Theorem 4) with exhaustive check of all laws on a^0..a^12 (EXP-C01-03); awaiting independent skeptic review
new.statement:
(End({a}*), pointwise juxtaposition, composition) is a commutative semiring isomorphic to (N, +, x) via
phi -> |phi(a)|. For two symbols modulo commutation, composition of endomorphisms is not commutative.
new.title: Multiplication emerges as composition of substitutions; with two symbols it is non-commutative

new.counterexample: u = aab, v = aba: the word baa is fixed by every rewrite, so its class {baa} is smaller than its counting class {aab, aba, baa}. All 33 relations of length 3-4 fail (EXP-C01-04).
new.statement:
For every relation u <-> v over {a,b} with u != v and equal symbol counts, the generated congruence
coincides with counting (Parikh) equivalence on all words of length >= |u|.
new.title: H-C01-4: a single rearranging relation generates counting equivalence on long words (refuted)

new.applications: Exact information content of words modulo an invisible local rewrite (e.g. log2(phi) bits/symbol modulo aab = aba).
new.novelty_basis: Combination of Newman's lemma, the critical-pair lemma and Guibas-Odlyzko (1981); analogue of a one-element Groebner basis (Bergman 1978). Probably folklore; pending Historian audit.
new.proof_check: written proof (proofs/paper/C01.md, Theorem 5); its overlap lemma is Lean-verified (common_border_joinable); corroborated by 756 + 1632 relations; awaiting independent skeptic review
new.statement:
Let u != v be words of length k over a q-letter alphabet with Borders(u) contained in Borders(v). Then
{u -> v} is convergent, the classes of length-n words modulo u = v correspond to the length-n words
avoiding u, and the class-count generating function is c_u(x) / (x^k + (1 - q x) c_u(x)), c_u the
autocorrelation polynomial of u. For unbordered u this is 1/(1 - q x + x^k); for q = 2 the counts are
partial sums of (k-1)-bonacci numbers (k = 3: F(n+3) - 1).
new.title: Border-containment theorem for one length-preserving relation

new.proof_check: computer-assisted (Python) - independently re-verified convergent completion, Aho-Corasick automaton, recurrence-order bound s+k; brute-force cross-check n <= 8; not Lean-checked
new.statement:
For each of the 1632 relations marked PROVEN in results/EXP-C01-07.json (binary k <= 6, ternary k <= 4),
the class-count generating function equals c(x)/(x^k + (1 - q x) c(x)), c the common-border polynomial.
new.title: Common-border formula proved for 1632 specific relations by verified finite completions

new.limitations: Proved only in the border-containment case and for 1632 individual relations; 527 small relations remain open (infinite completions).
new.novelty_basis: Two web searches (2026-10-18) found no general formula; related literature - Nyberg-Brodda survey of one-relation monoids (arXiv:2105.02853), "Relations on words" (arXiv:1602.03364), Kudryavtseva 2010. Needs a deeper search (Hilbert series of one-relator algebras - Anick, Piontkovski, Iyudu).
new.statement:
For all words u != v of equal length k over a q-letter alphabet, the number of congruence classes of
length-n words modulo u = v has generating function c(x) / (x^k + (1 - q x) c(x)), where
c(x) = 1 + sum over words b that are borders of both u and v of x^(k - |b|).
new.title: Common-border conjecture: one-relation class counts depend only on common borders

new: Exact partitions of 25 slices coincide with symbol-count partitions; completion of the swap relations is the finite system {yx -> xy | x < y} whose normal forms are sorted words.
All 6159 relation sets agree with index = min m_i and period = gcd(n_i - m_i) under two independent methods.
Substitutions on one symbol form (N, +, x); on two symbols modulo commutation composition is non-commutative (154/200 random pairs).

Every one of the 33 rearranging relations of length 3-4 has words whose class is strictly smaller than their counting class; H-C01-4 refuted. Unexpected regularity in the class counts (Fibonacci and tribonacci partial sums) triggered H-C01-5.
aab <-> aba: class of baa is {baa}, counting class {aab, aba, baa}
H-C01-5 holds for all 756 relations with an unbordered side; 81 of the 281 relations with both sides bordered deviate from the generic count, all sharing a common border.
The common-border formula (H-C01-7) holds for all 2159 relations tested, including 1326 hard relations not covered by Theorem 5.
1632 relations proved for all n by independently re-verified finite completions; 527 hard relations have infinite completions within the search bounds.
Parametric (regular) completions for the 527 open relations

assumptions: configurations = multisets of levels (C01)
new.falsification: Two different normal forms, unequal derivation lengths, a cycle, or a mismatch with base-b digits.
new.hypothesis: Every derivation terminates in the same configuration, namely the base-b digits of n, after exactly (n - s_b(n))/(b - 1) exchanges, s_b the base-b digit sum.
new.methodology: Exhaustive derivation graphs from n tokens (all orders of exchange) for small n; fast stabilisation compared with base-b digits for n <= 20000.
new.question: Starting from n tokens at level 0 (a unary numeral), what does the exchange rule b[k] -> [k+1] produce, and does the order of exchanges matter?
new.title: Integer bases as normal forms of the exchange rule b tokens -> 1 token one level up

assumptions: weights w_k = F(k+2)
unary starts n <= 40; all configurations of value <= 26
new.falsification: A cycle, two sinks, or a sink different from the greedy Zeckendorf representation.
new.hypothesis: H-C02-F: from every configuration the system terminates and reaches a unique normal form, the Zeckendorf representation of its value (weights 1,2,3,5,8,...); unlike the binary rule, derivation lengths depend on the order of exchanges.
new.methodology: Exhaustive derivation graphs (cycle detection, sinks, min/max lengths) from unary starts and from every configuration of small value.
new.question: With exchanges [k]+[k+1] -> [k+2], 2[k] -> [k+1]+[k-2] (and boundary versions), do all orders of exchange reach the Zeckendorf representation, and how long do they take?
new.title: Fibonacci exchange rules: termination, confluence and derivation lengths

assumptions: m in {2,3,4}, b_j in {0..3}, J <= 3 (last coefficient nonzero): 189 rules
unary starts n <= 200; representations for n <= 3000
new.falsification: A rule with sum b < m and an infinite derivation, a rule with sum b >= m terminating from all n <= 200 with no glider, or a radix-order inversion.
new.hypothesis: H-C02-1: the rule terminates from every unary start iff sum_j b_j < m (emergent base r > 1, r the positive root of sum_j b_j r^j = m); otherwise some start produces a periodic glider. H-C02-2: for terminating rules, n < n' implies rep(n) < rep(n') in radix order.
new.methodology: Batch-firing upward sweep. After level k is processed the future depends only on the window (c_{k+1}, ..., c_{k+J}); a repeated nonzero window is a certificate of an infinite derivation (periodic glider). Radix order = compare length, then digits from the top.
new.question: Which carry rules turn unary numerals into finite normal forms, what is the emergent base, and are the resulting representations ordered like ordinary numerals?
new.title: Carry-rule survey: termination criterion, glider certificates and emergent bases

new: Batch-firing upward sweep. After level k is processed the future depends only on the window (c_{k+1}, ..., c_{k+J}), and the window map is monotone; a window W with an entry >= m that is later dominated componentwise (periodic glider if equal) certifies infinitely many firings. Radix order = compare length, then digits from the top.
old: Batch-firing upward sweep. After level k is processed the future depends only on the window (c_{k+1}, ..., c_{k+J}); a repeated nonzero window is a certificate of an infinite derivation (periodic glider). Radix order = compare length, then digits from the top.

assumptions: the 31 terminating rules of EXP-C02-03
exact arithmetic in Q(r) modulo the minimal polynomial of r
all stable configurations with at most L levels (m^L <= 2e5)
new.falsification: Two stable configurations with the same integer value; a merged sum that stabilises to something other than rep(a+b).
new.hypothesis: H-C02-4: for every terminating carry rule (sum b < m), distinct stable configurations of length <= L have distinct values, so each integer has exactly one stable representation. H-C02-5: stab(rep(a) + rep(b)) = rep(a + b).
new.methodology: Enumerate every stable configuration up to L levels, reduce sum c_k x^k modulo the minimal polynomial of r, keep those whose value is an integer, group by value. Addition: 2000 random pairs per rule.
new.question: In a terminating carry system, can an integer have a stable representation other than the normal form of its unary numeral? Does merging two normal forms and stabilising add them?
new.title: Uniqueness of stable representations in emergent bases; addition by merging

assumptions: the 31 terminating rules
all stable configurations supported on gZ with at most L supported levels (m^L <= 2e5)
new.falsification: A collision for a primitive irreducible P~, or no collision for a non-primitive P~.
new.hypothesis: H-C02-4': let g = gcd{j : b_j > 0} and P~(y) = sum_i b_(gi) y^i - m. If P~ is primitive and irreducible over Q, distinct stable configurations supported on multiples of g have distinct values; if P~ is not primitive, two such configurations with equal value exist.
new.methodology: Exact integer evaluation modulo the minimal polynomial (as in EXP-C02-04) restricted to levels 0, g, 2g, ...; compare collisions with the primitive/irreducible prediction.
new.question: Exactly which terminating carry rules have unique stable representations?
new.title: Refined uniqueness: primitive irreducible carry polynomials on the reachable sublattice

assumptions: OEIS search API (responses cached in cache/oeis for reproducibility)
absence of a match is weak evidence of novelty only
new.falsification: An OEIS entry matching a sequence labelled potentially novel.
new.hypothesis: Integer-base and rational-base sequences are known; the Fibonacci exchange derivation lengths and representations in the emergent base r = 1.3028 (3[k] -> [k+1]+[k+2]) may not be.
new.methodology: Query the first terms of each sequence; if there is no hit, query a shifted window.
new.question: Are the sequences produced by exchange systems already catalogued?
new.title: Novelty checks of C02 sequences against the OEIS

new.novelty_basis: Chip-firing on a path / standard carrying.
new.proof_check: written proof (proofs/paper/C02.md Theorem 2) + exhaustive check of 134 derivation graphs and n <= 20000; awaiting independent skeptic review
new.statement:
From n tokens at level 0, every maximal derivation of the rule "b tokens at level k -> 1 token at level k+1"
(b >= 2) is finite, ends at the base-b expansion of n, and has exactly (n - s_b(n))/(b - 1) steps.
new.title: Integer bases emerge as normal forms of the exchange rule b[k] -> [k+1]

new.novelty_basis: Strong convergence of chip-firing (Bjorner-Lovasz-Shor 1991); abelian sandpile (Dhar 1990); abelian networks (Bond-Levine).
new.proof_check: written proof (proofs/paper/C02.md Theorem 1); awaiting independent skeptic review
new.statement:
For a carry rule m[k] -> sum_j b_j [k+j], one-step firings at different levels commute. Hence from any
configuration either all maximal derivations are infinite or all are finite with the same endpoint,
length and firing vector.
new.title: Abelian property of carry rules (order of exchanges is irrelevant)

new.proof_check: written proof (proofs/paper/C02.md Theorem 3); awaiting independent skeptic review
new.statement:
If sum_j b_j < m every derivation from every configuration terminates. If sum_j b_j > m, the emergent base
satisfies r < 1 and no derivation from n tokens at level 0 terminates when n > (m - 1)/(1 - r).
new.title: Termination dichotomy for carry rules away from sum b = m

new.limitations: Holds for all 28 surveyed rules (m <= 4, J <= 3, b_j <= 3); the general spreading step is unproved.
new.statement:
For every carry rule with sum_j b_j = m there is a unary start n whose sweep reaches a window dominating the
uniform-firing glider T = (T_1, ..., T_J), T_i = sum_{j >= i} b_j (or its g-sparse analogue, g the gcd of
the support of b); consequently its derivations from n are infinite. (Proved: T is a fixed point of the
window map and any window dominating T forces infinitely many firings.)
new.title: Carry rules with sum b = m never terminate from all unary starts (uniform glider)

new.proof_check: computer-assisted (Python) - explicit periodic-glider or monotone-pumping certificates for 158 rules; Theorem 3(a) for the 31 others
new.statement:
Among the 189 carry rules with m in {2,3,4}, J <= 3, b_j <= 3, exactly the 31 with sum b < m terminate from
every unary start; each of the other 158 has a unary start n <= 200 with an infinite derivation.
new.title: Termination classification for all 189 small carry rules (computer-assisted)

new.counterexample: 4[k] -> 2[k+1] (base 2 with digits 0..3): the stable configurations '2' and '10' both have value 2. Also 4[k] -> [k+2] on all levels, 4[k] -> 2[k+2], 4[k] -> 2[k+3] (EXP-C02-04).
new.statement: For every carry rule with sum b < m, each integer has exactly one stable configuration of that value.
new.title: H-C02-4: every terminating carry rule gives unique stable representations (refuted)

new.novelty_basis: Gauss-lemma uniqueness arguments are classical for canonical number systems and generalized radix representations (Kovacs, Petho; Akiyama et al.); generalises the uniqueness of rational-base representations (Akiyama-Frougny-Sakarovitch 2008). Probably known; pending Historian audit.
new.proof_check: Lean 4 + Mathlib for the polynomial core (digits_unique, exists_large_coeff; standard axioms only); reduction to the lattice and the converse by written proof
new.statement:
Let g = gcd{j : b_j > 0} and P~(y) = sum_i b_(gi) y^i - m. If P~ is primitive and irreducible over Q, then
distinct stable configurations supported on multiples of g have distinct values; in particular every n has
exactly one stable representation there, namely rep(n). If P~ is not primitive, two such configurations with
equal value exist.
new.title: Uniqueness of representations when the reduced carry polynomial is primitive and irreducible

new.proof_check: written proof (proofs/paper/C02.md Theorem 6); 0 inversions for 31 rules up to n = 3000; awaiting independent skeptic review
new.statement: For every carry rule with sum b < m and every n, rep(n) < rep(n+1) in radix order.
new.title: Exchange representations respect the radix order

new.novelty_basis: The Zeckendorf game (Baird-Smith, Epstein, Flint, Miller, arXiv:1809.04881) - termination and shortest game N - Z(N); OEIS A219641.
new.proof_check: written proof (proofs/paper/C02.md Theorem 8); exhaustive check of 2167 configurations; awaiting independent skeptic review
new.statement:
With weights 1,2,3,5,8,..., the exchanges [k]+[k+1] -> [k+2], 2[k] -> [k+1]+[k-2] (k >= 2), 2[1] -> [2]+[0],
2[0] -> [1] terminate from every configuration at the Zeckendorf representation of its value, and the
shortest derivation from n tokens at level 0 has n - z(n) steps (z(n) = number of Zeckendorf terms).
new.title: The Fibonacci exchange system terminates at the Zeckendorf representation; shortest derivation n - z(n)

new.novelty_basis: The longest Zeckendorf game is studied by Cusenza et al. and the Williams SMALL group; the value sequence was not found in the OEIS (2026-10-18). No closed form known to us.
new.proof_check: computer-assisted exhaustive search of the full derivation graph (EXP-C02-02)
new.title: Longest Fibonacci exchange derivations (longest Zeckendorf games) for n <= 40

new: Binary..quinary carrying from unary numerals is order-independent; normal forms are base-b expansions and every complete derivation has (n - s_b(n))/(b - 1) exchanges.
The Fibonacci exchange system reaches the Zeckendorf representation from every tested configuration; derivation lengths vary between n - z(n) and a larger maximum.

Termination from unary starts holds exactly for the 31 rules with sum b < m; every one of the 158 other rules has a periodic-glider or monotone-pumping certificate; no radix-order inversion up to n = 3000.
H-C02-4 refuted - four terminating rules have integers with several stable representations; merge-and-stabilise addition always agrees with rep(a+b).
4[k] -> 2[k+1]: configurations 2 (two tokens at level 0) and 10 (one token at level 1) are both stable with value 2
Uniqueness holds for all 28 rules whose reduced carry polynomial is primitive and irreducible (over all stable configurations, not only integer-valued ones) and fails for the 3 non-primitive ones.

Base 3/2 = A024629 and shortest Fibonacci derivations = A219641 (rediscoveries); longest Fibonacci derivations and exotic-base representations have no OEIS match. The A089881 hit for representation lengths is a spurious shifted-window coincidence.
